walkthroughs.body_html:
Solid salt does not conduct electricity. Molten or dissolved salt does.

To conduct, you need charged particles that can move. In solid NaCl the ions are locked in a lattice. Melt it or dissolve it in water and the ions are free to flow.

Metals conduct because their delocalised electrons are free to drift through the structure, carrying charge.

Diamond does not conduct: every carbon uses all 4 outer electrons in bonds, so nothing is free. Graphite does conduct: each carbon uses only 3 bonds, leaving 1 delocalised electron per atom.

Use the periodic table as a shortcut.

Metal + non-metal = ionic (e.g. Na + Cl). Two non-metals = covalent (e.g. C + O). Two metals = metallic alloy (e.g. Cu + Zn = brass). The further apart on the table, the more ionic the bond.

mcqs.q: Solid sodium chloride does NOT conduct electricity because:
options: It has no charged particles
Its ions cannot move
Its electrons are shared
It is a non-metal
Metal atoms themselves move to carry the current.
Metals contain naturally moving protons that act as charge carriers.
Delocalised electrons are free to move through the lattice of positive ions, carrying charge.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.

mcqs.q: What happens to electrons when sodium reacts with chlorine?
options: Sodium and chlorine share an electron between them.
Sodium loses one electron to chlorine; the resulting Na+ and Cl- ions attract electrostatically.
Graphite conducts because it can melt easily at room temperature.
Protons move from chlorine to sodium to balance the charges.
